label: Person
name: Albert Henry Ottenweller
summary:
Albert Henry Ottenweller (1916–2016) was an American Catholic bishop who served as Bishop of Steubenville in Ohio, reaching the exceptional age of 99 as one of the longest-lived American Catholic bishops of the twentieth century. Born in Ohio, he was ordained a priest of the Diocese of Toledo and was consecrated Bishop of Steubenville in 1977.

Steubenville's diocese was notable in the late twentieth century for its connection to charismatic Catholic renewal, particularly through Franciscan University of Steubenville, which became one of the most prominent centres of orthodox Catholic higher education and charismatic spirituality in the United States. Ottenweller's episcopate spanned the height of this renewal and contributed to the diocese's distinctive spiritual character.

His longevity—he lived well past his retirement, dying in 2016—made him a living link between the pre-Vatican II Church and the twenty-first century. He was ordained a priest in 1944, just before the end of World War II, and lived long enough to see the papacy of Pope Francis. His pastoral style was described as gentle and personally devout, representative of the post-conciliar American bishop who sought to implement Vatican II's reforms while maintaining traditional Catholic devotional life.
